audit.whatIsWrong: The two chart layers disagreed with each other AND with the whys prose. win[0..3] and phases[0..3].side said Yorick while whys[0..3] all say 'even', 'skill-based', 'neutral standoff'; win[4]/phases[4].side said Skill while whys[4] says level 6 tilts to you. The packet chart is Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yorick/Yorick/Yorick, and the nasus__yorick mirror explicitly notes phases[0..4].side oversell Yorick.
audit.why: Neither champion has a kill threat before six — Nasus wants to touch minions, Yorick wants to bank graves. Yorick's real swing is Eulogy of the Isles at 6, which lets the Maiden hold the wave and starve Siphoning Strike stacks. The prose already said this; only the side fields were wrong.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Yorick / Yorick / Yorick across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side as one paired group, ratings 5/5/5/5/6/7/7. whys[] needed no change — they already matched the corrected chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike carried a cooldown number, and phases[4]/phases[6] gave no reason tied to either ultimate.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80s and grants bonus Armor and Magic Resistance while it rages, so the fight timing is 'after it ends', not 'whenever'. Eulogy of the Isles at 160s rank 1 is the actual lane-swinging spike because the Maiden holds the wave and denies stacks even when Yorick leaves.
audit.corrected: phases[4], phases[5], phases[6] and breakdown.cooldowns keyed to Fury of the Sands' 120s and Wither's 15s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer said only 'His only kite. Bait it before committing.' — no ranges, no cooldowns, no mention that Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset or that Fury of the Sands is percent-health.
audit.why: Wither is 700 range on 15/14/13/12/11s and decays both move AND attack speed, which is what actually breaks a Yorick swing mid-trade — the standard 'it's a slow' framing understates it. Siphoning Strike is a 255-range auto reset on 7.5s falling to 3.5s, so the wind-up is the tell rather than the cast. Fury of the Sands does percent-health damage and grants him bonus Armor and Magic Resistance, so stacking raw armour is the wrong response and Grievous Wounds against Soul Eater's lifesteal is the right one. Mourning Mist reduces armour, which is the direct counter to the resistances he gains under his ultimate.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, report[5].t, phases[2].why and breakdown.late rewritten with Wither's 15s and dual slow, Siphoning Strike's reset, and Fury of the Sands' percent-health plus resistance gain.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late said 'anti-heal stays core' without saying why armour is the wrong buy.
audit.why: The _missing feed's resistances-invalidated rule applies: Fury of the Sands is percent-health, so armour does not scale against it, while Soul Eater is pure lifesteal that Grievous Wounds does answer.
audit.corrected: breakdown.late and phases[6].why now name percent health and Soul Eater explicitly.
